criticalRisks: SILENT MODEL SUBSTITUTION (correctness): legacy-fabric-bridge.mjs legacyPacketToFabricJob never includes packet.model in the returned job. Every catch-all packet (any model without a claude-/gpt-/gemini- prefix, including the default nvidia/nemotron-3-nano-30b-a3b) is served by whatever the fabric selects. The caller receives a completion with no error or indication of substitution.

EXPLICIT nvidia-inference-team OVERRIDE HITS EXHAUSTED PILOT (correctness): run-one-exchange.mjs deriveTeam() — fabric bridge fires only when routing.basis==='model-prefix-default'. A packet with params.provider='nvidia-inference-team' gets basis='explicit-override' and is sent directly to the exhausted nvidia child team harness, bypassing the fabric and producing a pilot-cap refusal.

spawnSync SERIALIZES ALL complete() CALLS (throughput): inference.mjs:39 — spawnSync blocks the event loop for the full child-process wall time. No two complete() calls can overlap in one process. This is per-request synchronous waiting; cross-process concurrency is unaffected but the caller must manage it externally.

EXCHANGES_DIR NOT CREATED BEFORE FIRST WRITE (correctness): run-one-exchange.mjs writeAndReport — countSeatedExchanges() silently returns 0 when content/exchanges/ is absent, so the pilot-cap check passes. But writeFileSync in writeAndReport throws if the directory does not exist, crashing the harness after inference completes; the parent sees an unparseable-output refusal.

concurrency:1 SERIALIZES PROVIDER FAILOVER IN FABRIC DISPATCH (throughput): run-one-exchange.mjs — dispatchJobs is called with concurrency:1 even when registry.attempts names multiple endpoints. If the fabric supports parallel provider probing for a single job, this cap forces strictly serial fallover, suppressing cross-provider throughput within one exchange.
